verdict.rationale: Sentry's source is publicly readable on GitHub, and the self-hosting docs say you can run all of Sentry on your own server for free. One user also credits its open-source nature with letting them read the code directly. However, another user in the same thread calls a licensing development a move toward closed-source software, so whether the license is genuinely open is unclear, and the evidence never names the actual license. Missing for 10: an explicit license statement from Sentry's docs or repo, and confirmation that the current license is an OSI-approved open license.
